articles.headline: Stolen! (notice)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: On last Monday morning, the 30th ult., while sitting at the breakfast table, some thief slipped into the hall, and abstracted from off the rack my best Coat, containing, in the side pocket, our Diary for 1861, with every-day accounts inscribed therein, and a note for $107 ... my Elder's Orders, given me by Bishop Quinn, and a variety of other papers. ... Elisha Weaver, No. 619 Pine Street, Phila.

articles.headline: Free-will offering on the National Fast Day (notice)
articles.author: E. Weaver
articles.summary: The following churches have responded to our call in relation to the free-will offering in Philadelphia on Thursday, the 26th ultimo. Pretty much all the colored churches, in obedience to the proclamation of the President of the United States, held divine service. We had services in Big Bethel church, both during the day and at night ... We received the sum of but Ten Dollars and Fifty-four Cents ($10.54) from that large body of people of over two thousand persons.

articles.headline: Loyalty and Disloyalty (letter)
articles.author: John M. Brown
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--I may be pardoned for obtruding myself upon the columns of your excellent paper. ... I have read all your articles published in the Recorder, but the one in to-day's issue takes me all aback. Signed John M. Brown, Baltimore, Sept. 21st, 1861 (address line partly illegible). A defence of Bishop Nazrey's position as bishop of the B.M.E. Church in Canada against the editor's charge of 'disloyalty'; cites the letter of Rev. A. R. Green to the Indiana Conference and the 1860 Pittsburgh General Conference.

articles.headline: Two Cent Money (editorial)
articles.author: E. Weaver
articles.summary: The General Conference has laid down the plan by which all preachers who go to our Annual Conferences, in accordance with the vow of being received into the itinerant service ... Now, the raising of the two cent money is to all intents and purposes, a part of that duty ... One thing we do know, and that is we have not received any two cent money--monthly nor quarterly.

articles.headline: Sabbath School Celebration (Burlington Circuit)
articles.author: Joseph Thompson
articles.summary: The annual celebration of the several Sabbath Schools, on the Burlington Circuit, came off on the 29th August, in a very pleasant and convenient woods near Evesham meeting house. Brother Joseph Smith, the elder in charge, was there, in company with several others of our brethren. ... After listening to the speeches of several persons, and witnessing the presentation of a banner to Milford School ... Joseph Thompson, Evesham, Sept. 24th, 1861.

articles.headline: Observance of the National Fast (editorial)
articles.summary: The day of prayer and fasting appointed by the President seems to have been observed very generally throughout the land. In all the Eastern cities, secular business was for the most part suspended ... We conclude this article by giving several extracts from the Philadelphia Press. (Extracts from sermons by white Philadelphia ministers, incl. Rev. T. J. Shepherd; not linked.)

articles.headline: What Does the Editor Mean? (letter)
articles.summary: Dear Brethren:--I have no disposition to engage in a controversy. ... I rejoice that the article on 'Loyalty and Disloyalty' has effected some good. ... My learned and much esteemed brother of the Baltimore District, Rev. J. M. B[rown], ... Unsigned reply in the Nazrey controversy.

articles.headline: Bishopric of the United States and Canada (letter)
articles.summary: Dear Brother Editor:--From reading your last number, I see that the Bishopric of the A. M. E. Church and B. M. E. Church is still in controversy ... Signed with a pseudonym (illegible: 'Pembroke'?), Mount Pisgah, October 1st, 1861. Argues Bishop Nazrey was rightly Bishop of Canada after the 1856 General Conference.

articles.headline: Our Wants (editorial)
articles.summary: We are still looking anxiously towards every quarter to see if the brethren will respond to our wants. We must have $200, by or before the 25th of November coming. ... There are some forty or fifty, if not more, of our ministers, who have been taking the Recorder nearly ten months, and have neither sent their own subscriptions, nor anything else.

articles.headline: The President and the Colored People (letter)
articles.author: J. P. C.
articles.summary: On the 12th of August, 1861, the President of these United States issued a proclamation setting apart the last Thursday in September, as a day of humiliation, prayer and fasting for all the people of the nation ... Could the fast be an acceptable one to the Lord, under existing circumstances, with the exclusion of black men? ... J. P. C., Trenton, Oct. 1st, 1861.

articles.headline: The National Fast and the Negro (editorial)
articles.summary: The present rebellion has grown out of the desire of the rebels to perpetuate the institution of slavery in this country.

Any subscriber not receiving his paper regularly will please notify us of the neglect without delay ... articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--By your issue of the 12th of October, you still persist in your idea that those who differ from you are 'Disloyal' ... John M. Brown, No. 64 Henrietta St., Baltimore, Oct. 12th, 1861 [address read through blur]. Weaver, has issued a call to the ministers and members of the same for aid and comfort, toward the support of our book concern, and the Christian Recorder ... This call ... has been seconded by the editor of the Recorder, Rev. A. L. Stanford ... we do hereby appoint, that on the evening of the 4th Sabbath in October, being the 27th day of the same, subscriptions will be taken, and a general collection lifted, in Mount Zion church, for the book concern.

articles.headline: New Stove Store! (editorial notice of William Still's store)
articles.summary: We take pleasure in calling the attention of our readers to the new stove store recently opened by our friend, Wm. Still, at 107 North 5th St. We can not but see he is as fully prepared to meet the demands of our people, or indeed the public generally, who may want good cook, parlor or chamber stoves, as the generality of stove dealers in this city. His variety is large and of the most approved patterns, at reasonable prices. Likewise in the repairing line ... Most assuredly we wish him success, feeling fully persuaded that the more our people can establish themselves in respectable business localities ...
people: proprietor, new stove store, 107 North Fifth Street (printed 'Wm. Still')

articles.headline: Bishop's Support (editorial)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: Many of the members and preachers of the Philadelphia District seem to stumble at raising and paying the Bishop's Support, and, indeed, many have said they would not raise any thing, and some members say they will not pay any thing for the Bishop who presides over this district, viz.: Bishop Nazrey. ... Our advice is this: The money should be paid into the hands of the preachers in charge ... until Conference meets ... We would also recommend to the brethren of the New England Conference to pursue the same course.

articles.headline: 'Loyalty and Disloyalty' (editorial reply to Rev. J. M. B.)
articles.summary: Why not read the question as it is? My learned opponent of the Baltimore District, Rev. J. M. B., for some reason seems inclined to misrepresent the editorial views on the question 'Loyalty and Disloyalty' ... (Reply to John M. Brown on the Indiana Conference's disapproval of Bishop Nazrey's course in Canada.) Also on this page: 'The Rev. J. M. B.'s Interrogatories Answered' (a further letter, Frederick?, Md.).

articles.headline: Religious Union (letter)
articles.author: Singleton T. Jones
articles.summary: Dear Brother in Christ:--Having been kindly invited by the pastor of 'Bethel Church,' in your city, to fill his pulpit on the evening of the recent National Fast Day; and having chosen a text which contained a promise of the advancement and glory of the church of Christ, I took occasion to remark that, I regarded it the duty, as well as the interest of the colored Methodists in the United States, to seek in every possible way ... to bring about a union of all the elements of Methodism among us ... Singleton T. Jones, Harrisburg, Pa., Oct. 11th? 1861.

articles.headline: Donation to Rev. T. H. Cooper, A.M.E. Church, Woodbury, N.J.
articles.summary: A donation was given by the ladies connected with the A. M. E. Church, Woodbury, N. J., on Thursday evening, the 17th inst., for the benefit of their pastor, brother T. H. Cooper. An appropriate address was delivered on the occasion, by the Rev. Shepherd Holcomb. After which the value of $[40?] was presented to the pastor, $18.65 in cash, and the balance in such necessaries as are suitable for family use. The committee of arrangements, in behalf of the ladies connected with this church, were, Mrs. Comfort? Pall [VERIFY], Mrs. Elizabeth Lawe [VERIFY], Miss C. Peterson, Miss Anna? Lawe [VERIFY].

articles.headline: Editorial note on the Philadelphia and New England Districts and the bishopric
articles.summary: We call the attention of our readers to an article in the present number, entitled, 'District of Columbia Correspondence,' and particularly that portion of it which relates to the Bishopric. Our Correspondent tells us that Rev. J. M. B. and the Presbyter are the exponents of both the ministry and laity in the Baltimore District. Have the Philadelphia and New England Districts, who claim Bishop Nazrey as their Bishop for the time being, no voice to advocate their rights?

articles.headline: Bishop's Appointments

In the evening of the same Sabbath, at the Union A. M. E. Church. From the 15th to the 22d of November, he will be on the Berks County Circuit. He will then leave for Freehold Circuit ... From thence he will proceed to Allentown Circuit.

articles.headline: Haytien Emigration (letter)
articles.author: G. W. G.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--I have watched your paper for some weeks to see whether some one would not 'come out' upon the last (but not least) move upon Emigration to Hayti. But as no one has said anything so far, and as I think the only thing wanting is to set the ball in motion, I take the liberty of dropping you a line in reference thereto. (Dated Phila., Oct. 28, 1861; complains that paid Haytian agents avoid holding meetings in Philadelphia.)

articles.headline: Obituary of Mrs. Catherine Wiggins
articles.summary: Seldom are we called upon to record the death of one who possessed in so great a degree all those Christian virtues which adorn the followers of Christ, as was seen in the character of our departed sister. Catherine Wiggins, the subject of this commemorative, departed this life on Sabbath evening, June 16th, 1861, in the forty-seventh year of her age. Sister Wiggins' funeral sermon was delivered in Bethel Church, by the Rev. James Frisby [VERIFY], on Sabbath afternoon, October 20th.
people: deceased, June 16, 1861, age 47; member of Bethel Church (professed religion 1840 as printed); left children

articles.summary: The fall series of quarterly meetings have just been concluded for these two circuits. These were most precious seasons of refreshing from the presence of the Lord, to all believers who were present to enjoy them. The first meeting of the series was held in Mount Zion church, in the city of Trenton, on the first Saturday and Sunday in October. (Dated Phila., Nov. 7th, 1861.)

On the 21st of September, at the Quarterly Meeting, (the meeting was continued seventeen nights in succession,) twenty-one persons, backsliders included, turned their backs against the powers of darkness ... thirty-two persons had their names enrolled on the class-books. (Dated New Brunswick, Nov. 6, 1861.)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting (Frankford)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: At Frankford, on Sabbath, the 10th inst., we attended Father Robertson's Quarterly Meeting. At 9 o'clock, A. M., was celebrated the love-feast, and we don't know when we heard Christians speak so much to the purpose as they did on that occasion. Father Robertson said that the old residents of the place thought they never saw such a time. At 11 o'clock, A. M., Rev. Josiah Eddy gave us a very interesting discourse.

articles.headline: A Revival (Union Church, Coates Street)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Mr. Editor--I am happy to inform you and all the lovers of Christianity that we held an anxious meeting in the A. M. E. Union Church, located in Coates street, in Philadelphia. The meeting commenced on the 7th of October, and terminated on the 11th of November; and during that period the blessed God who reigns in heaven visited the aforesaid church with a wonderful outpouring of his divine Spirit, which resulted in adding to said church thirty-five persons, male and female, twenty-six of whom professed to be soundly converted to God.

articles.headline: Obituary: Elizabeth Jackson
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Departed this life, [month and day illegible], 1861, in the triumphs of Christian faith, after a long and lingering illness, that venerable and aged servant of God, Elizabeth Jackson, late consort of Benjamin Jackson. She was born in Newland [VERIFY] Township, Chester Co., Pa., July 6th, 1782. (Signed J. P. Campbell, Trenton, Nov. 12th, 1861.)
people: deceased 1861, aged 79 years and 25 days; b. July 6, 1782, Chester Co., Pa.; member of Zoar Church, Northern Liberties, until 18[3?9], then among the founders of the A. M. E. Union Church, Coates St., said to have paid its first cash subscription; Sabbath school visitor

articles.headline: A Word to Our Readers
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: We recently took occasion to peep in at the old Anti-Slavery Office, No. 107 North Fifth Street, Philadelphia, and found that our friend, Mr. William Still, who was clerk in the former office, has converted the greater part of it into a fine stove store. His stock is extensive and superior, and he is prepared to accommodate the public at the shortest notice. In the same building we noticed the promising store of Mrs. E. A. Palmer. Her department consists in Trimmings, Hosiery, Shirt-making, Dress-making, &c. ... These are both colored persons.
people: stove store, 107 North Fifth Street (former clerk of the Anti-Slavery Office)
trimmings, hosiery, shirt- and dress-making store, same building; on Government work, employing ten or twelve hands

articles.headline: Right and Wrong
articles.author: Willis Nazrey
articles.summary: To the numerous readers of the Christian Recorder:--In the 45th number, I promised to give you a history of the whole affair relative to myself and the B. M. E. Church. In accordance with the same, please see Committee's Report in No. 46, or the article entitled, 'An Informal Meeting of the Members of the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church.' Now I am willing for all men to think and judge for themselves.

articles.headline: The Bishopric (letter)
articles.author: Observer
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--As some persons are liable to be misled by a very fallacious argument used in the columns of your paper, in relation to Bishop Nazrey's membership in the A. M. E. Church, in saying that the General Conference did not make a law for him to act in the States, &c., I give you for the benefit of your readers, the following ... (signed 'Observer'; argues Nazrey never left the A. M. E. Church; replies to 'Mr. Presbyter').

articles.headline: Opposition to Haytien Emigration
articles.author: T. Strother
articles.summary: Mr. Editor--I see in Vol. 1, No. 46, of your paper, some allusion by 'G. W. G.' to the subject of Haytian Emigration. Sir, I have, for one, always felt opposed to that scheme, ever since I first heard the subject mooted. I consider it a full second-cousin to the Colonization scheme, which I ever hated from its infancy. (No place given.)

articles.headline: Appointment (funeral sermon of Sister Elizabeth Williams)
articles.summary: The funeral sermon of Sister Elizabeth Williams, deceased, will be delivered in the Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst Street, on Sabbath afternoon, the 8th instant, at 3 o'clock, by Divine permission.

articles.headline: Notice (Executive Committee to meet in Philadelphia)
articles.summary: The Executive Committee will meet in Philadelphia, at 9 o'clock, A. M., on the 18th instant.

articles.headline: Notice (funeral obsequies of Rev. Walter Proctor)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: The funeral obsequies of Rev. Walter Proctor will be held in Bethel Church, Sixth Street, on Monday, the 16th instant, at 12 o'clock, P. M., that being the day appointed for his interment.

articles.headline: Obituary (Rev. Walter Proctor)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: As we were on our way home from our tour East, and had just entered the city of Philadelphia, directing our steps towards our homestead, the sad intelligence smote mournfully on our ears that Father Proctor was dead! ... 'Rev. Walter Proctor is dead. He departed this life on the 10th instant, at 7 o'clock, A. M., at his late residence in Rodman Street, in the 71st year of his age.'
people: deceased (Rev.); died 10 Dec 1861 at his residence in Rodman Street, 71st year; member of Bethel Church about 48 years; ordained Deacon by Richard Allen
ordained Proctor a Deacon (Rev.; 'the first Bishop of the A. M. E. Church'), mentioned

articles.headline: To Our Readers (A. L. Stanford indisposed)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: We are again at home, after our eventful tour, and at our post. The Rev. A. L. Stanford has been somewhat indisposed for several days back, not having been able to attend to his editorial duties properly for some two or three weeks.

articles.headline: Obituary: Death of Mrs. Eliza Burton
articles.author: E. M. F.
articles.summary: Died, Nov. 20th [VERIFY day], 1861, Mrs. Eliza Burton [VERIFY], consort of Mr. George M. Burton [VERIFY]. It may be truly said that a great woman has fallen in Zion, for she was a worthy member in the Central Presbyterian Church,--useful both spiritually and temporally. She was for many years a leader of the female Prayer Meeting in said Church.

articles.headline: Letter on Bishop Nazrey and the B. M. E. Church (reply to 'Observer')
articles.author: [pseudonym, unread; dated Mount Pisgah, Pa., Dec. 3d? 1861]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--I had supposed after Bishop Nazrey's elaborate answer to the ministers of the Philadelphia Conference, that there would be no further arguments needed to convince an intelligent public that the question is settled.

articles.headline: Religious Notices (Burlington Circuit quarterly meetings)
articles.author: J. H. Smith
articles.summary: Quarterly meetings of the Burlington Circuit. On the first Sabbath in January, at Burlington; second Sabbath at Mount Holly; third Sabbath at Evesham; fourth Sabbath at Milford. On the first Sabbath in February, at Snow Hill; second Sabbath at Jordantown. J. H. Smith, Elder in charge.

articles.headline: Appointment (Bishop Nazrey at Wesley A. M. E. Church)
articles.summary: In the Wesley A. M. E. Church, on Sunday evening the 22d inst., at 7 o'clock, by the Bishop, Rev. Willis Nazrey.

articles.headline: Notice (Rev. Elisha Weaver to preach at Union Church, Coates Street)
articles.summary: Hereafter all matter pertaining to or intended for the Christian Recorder, must be directed to Rev. Elisha Weaver. ... The Rev. Elisha Weaver will preach in Union Church, Coates Street, on Sabbath, at 3 o'clock, P. M.

articles.headline: Notice to Our City Subscribers
articles.summary: Our city subscribers will, for the future, pay their $2.00, in advance, to us, or at our office; and then the carriers will have nothing to do but to collect one penny for their services.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: Isaac Evans, Darby, Pa., by the hands of Mrs. Harris, $2 00; Rev. H. M. Turner, of Baltimore, for papers, 3 00; Rev. W. R. Revels, of Indianapolis, Ind., for Book Concern, 5 00; ...

articles.headline: Letter from Brother Smith
articles.author: James W. Smith
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--Having been one among the first of the subscribers of the Recorder, (I have not troubled you with any communication before,) permit me to insert a few lines to the ministry in reason to their duties to God, to themselves, and to their fellow man.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 27th of October, by Rev. Samuel Murray, Mr. Leven Pota [VERIFY] to Miss Margaret Conley [VERIFY], all of this city. On last Sabbath evening, by Rev. Elisha Weaver, Mr. Stephen Searle [VERIFY] to Miss Anna Hanson [VERIFY], all of this city.

articles.headline: Resignation (A. L. Stanford; Elisha Weaver named editor)
articles.summary: Rev. A. L. Stanford, who has been acting editor of this paper since the 15th of July, 1861, handed in his resignation to the Committee on the 18th instant, which was accepted by them, and took effect on the same day. His reasons for doing so he will himself assign.
people: named Editor and General Book Steward

articles.headline: Notice (Annals of the First African Church ... St. Thomas)
articles.summary: We find upon our table a Christmas treat, which is entitled, 'Annals of the First African Church in the United States of America, now styled the African Episcopal Church of St. Thomas.' This is a new work, just compiled by the Rev. William Douglass, Rector of St. Thomas' Church, Philadelphia, Pa. The book comprises 172 pages.
people: compiler of the Annals; Rector of St. Thomas' Church, Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: News from the Churches (Frankford Circuit; Trenton)
articles.summary: Rev. William Jackson, of Vincennes, Ind., writes that the Lord is powerfully pouring out his Spirit upon his circuit. ... Rev. Richard Robertson, of the Frankford Circuit, has been, we are informed, holding a protracted meeting for several weeks, which has resulted to the good of many precious souls. It is said that there never was such a work in Frankford before. Rev. J. P. Campbell, of Trenton, we are informed, is having a shower of God's blessing poured out in Trenton.

articles.headline: To the Ministers and Pastors of the A. M. E. Church of Phila.
articles.summary: Will you not appoint special meetings, or call your Church and people together, and procure their subscription for the Christian Recorder? Of course you have influence over them, and they are looking for you to bring it before them.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: From the hands of Mr. J. H. Pierce, of Gouldtown, N. J., in full for his subscription to the 1st of January, 1862, $1 00; Miss H. Jackson, of Springfield, Ill., 1 00; John Lee, [Springfield, Ill.] 1 00; Rodman Dutton [VERIFY], of Burlington, N. J., 1 00; Miss Matilda Toneyah [VERIFY], of Bristol, N. J., 1 00; Peter Toneyah [VERIFY], [Bristol, N. J.] 1 00.

articles.headline: Notice to All Subscribers of the Christian Recorder
articles.summary: Friends--We take this opportunity of informing you that your subscription for the Recorder ends on the first day of January, 1862. We sincerely thank you for your kind patronage, and hope that you have been benefited.

articles.headline: An Appeal to the Citizens of Philadelphia, and especially to our White Friends, in behalf of the Christian Recorder
articles.summary: The Christian Recorder is the only religious paper published in this country by colored people for the dissemination of the gospel of the blessed Jesus, as also of morality, literature, and science. We appeal to your generosity to contribute a New Year's gift, to the amount of two, three, five, or ten dollars to this enterprise.

articles.headline: Episcopal Visits
articles.author: Willis Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--This sketch was due some time since, but I have been otherwise hindered from giving it. According to appointment on the 23d of November I met Rev. J. Young, at the Montrose station, but owing to some little typographical error, I did not get to that appointment.

articles.headline: Marriage at the close of Bishop Nazrey's Episcopal Visits
articles.author: Willis Nazrey
articles.summary: We arrived the next day, the 28th of November, to ...ville, and preached there in the evening and administered the Lord's Supper,--after which I joined in the bonds of matrimony the following named persons: Mr. James Hay [VERIFY], of Freehold, N. J., to Miss Sarah Jane Williams, of ...ville [VERIFY], N. J.

events.name: United Beneficial Sisters of Rev. Joshua Woodlin's Society -- quarterly meeting called
events.location: Wealthy Dorsey's, Rodman St., between Ninth and Tenth, Philadelphia
events.description: NOTICE. The United Beneficial Sisters of Rev. Joshua Woodlin's Society are requested to attend their regular Stated Quarterly Meeting, on the 10th of October, 1861, at Wealthy Dorsey's, Rodman St., between Ninth and Tenth, at half past 7 o'clock, P.M. Punctual attendance is requested. By order of the President. Elizabeth Harris [VERIFY], Prest.; Eliza Stokely, Sec.
attendees: host; meeting held at her house, Rodman St. between Ninth and Tenth

events.name: National Fast Day services and free-will offerings in Philadelphia AME churches
events.location: Big Bethel; A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst street; Union Church ('up town'), Philadelphia
events.description: Reported by E. Weaver (General Book Steward). On the national fast day proclaimed by President Lincoln, 'pretty much all the colored churches' of Philadelphia held divine service. Big Bethel held services day and night; the claims of the Book Concern were set forth and a free-will offering of $10.54 was raised from a congregation of over two thousand. At 3 P.M. the same day Weaver was at the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst street ('though small in numbers, they have souls'), which raised $8.03. Union Church, situated 'up town', held two meetings and raised $3.14. Weaver asks every preacher in charge to take up a special collection and forward it.

events.name: Burlington Circuit Sabbath School celebration, Evesham
events.location: Woods near Evesham meeting house, Burlington Circuit, N.J.
events.description: Annual celebration of the several Sabbath Schools of the Burlington Circuit (Philadelphia Conference, N.J.). Brother Joseph Smith, elder in charge, attended with several other brethren. Day rainy; five schools [reading 'five' VERIFY], with more parents and friends than usual. Schools represented by their superintendents; speeches; a banner presented to Milford School, with singing and recitation by that school. Reported by Joseph Thompson, Evesham, Sept. 24th, 1861.

events.name: Quarterly meeting and love-feast, A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst street
events.location: A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Meeting Sunday 13 October 1861: service at 10 1/2 A.M.; preaching at 3 P.M. by Rev. Brother Orr; at 7 1/2 P.M. by Rev. S. Holcomb. Love-feast Monday evening 14 October, doors open 7 1/2, close half-past eight. A. L. Stanford, pastor.

events.name: Quarterly meeting, A.M.E. Church on Coates street
events.description: Quarterly Meeting in the A.M.E. Church on Coates street, 19 and 20 October 1861. Henry Davis, Minister.

events.name: Trenton Circuit collection for the Book Concern (two-cent money), Mount Zion church
events.description: Rev. J. P. Campbell, pastor of the Trenton Circuit, appointed the evening of the 4th Sabbath in October (27 October 1861) for subscriptions and a general collection in Mount Zion church, Trenton, for the A.M.E. Book Concern and the Christian Recorder, to raise Trenton's share of the 'two cent money', in response to the call of the General Book Steward Rev. E. Weaver, seconded by editor Rev. A. L. Stanford. Campbell would preach in Trenton that evening, returning from his quarterly meeting that day at Lawrenceville [reading VERIFY]. Princeton circuit to follow.

events.name: Quarterly meeting, A.M.E. Bethel Church, Sixth Street
events.location: A.M.E. Bethel Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia
events.description: Bethel quarterly meeting: General Class Friday evening 25 Oct. 7 1/2; preaching Saturday evening 26 Oct. 7 1/2; Sabbath 27 Oct.: band love feast 5 A.M., preaching 10 A.M., 3 P.M., and 7 1/2 P.M. by Rev. A. L. Stanford (Elder of the A.M.E. Church, Hurst St.); love feast Monday evening 28 Oct. 7 1/2. J. Woodlin, pastor.
attendees: preacher; elder, Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst St.

events.name: Memorial discourse for Mrs. Ann Jackson, Coates Street A.M.E. Church
events.description: 3 P.M. discourse, 'The life and death of Mrs. Ann Jackson,' by Rev. J. R. V. Morgan. Henry Davis, elder in charge.

events.name: Memorial discourse for Mrs. Elizabeth Jackson, Coates Street A.M.E. Church
events.description: 3 P.M. discourse, 'The life, character, and death of Mrs. Elizabeth Jackson,' by Rev. Jabez P. Campbell. Henry Davis, elder in charge.

events.name: National Fast Day evening sermon at Bethel by Rev. Singleton T. Jones
events.description: Per his letter 'Religious Union' (dated Harrisburg, Pa.), Singleton T. Jones was invited by the pastor of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, to fill the pulpit on the evening of the National Fast Day (26 Sept. 1861) and preached on the advancement of the church, urging union of all colored Methodist bodies in the United States. Jones (Harrisburg; A.M.E. Zion) is non-Philadelphia and is not linked.

events.name: Donation visit for Rev. T. H. Cooper, A.M.E. Church, Woodbury, N.J.
events.description: Donation given by the ladies of the Woodbury A.M.E. Church for their pastor T. H. Cooper; address by Rev. Shepherd Holcomb; goods valued at $[40?] presented, $18.65 in cash and the balance in family necessaries. Committee of arrangements: Mrs. Comfort? Pall [VERIFY], Mrs. Elizabeth Lawe [VERIFY], Miss C. Peterson, Miss Anna? Lawe [VERIFY].

events.name: Bishop Nazrey preaches at Bethel and Union churches
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia (10 A.M.); Union A. M. E. Church (evening)
events.description: Bishop Nazrey appointed to preach at Bethel, Sixth St., 10 A.M. Sunday Nov. 10, and at the Union A. M. E. Church that evening; then Berks County Circuit (Nov. 15-22), Freehold Circuit, and Allentown Circuit. Ministers of those circuits asked to make preaching appointments for him.

events.name: Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst St. -- Sunday services incl. memorial sermon for Cornelia B. Pagans [VERIFY]
events.location: A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst St., Philadelphia
events.description: Morning preaching (existence and unity of God); afternoon sermon by the (unnamed) pastor on the conversion and death of Cornelia B. Pagans [VERIFY]; evening sermon preparatory to the Eucharist by Rev. Joshua Woodlin, Elder of Bethel Church. Hours as printed partly uncertain (10 1/2 and 3 o'clock).

events.name: Funeral sermon for Catherine Wiggins at Bethel Church
events.description: Funeral sermon for Sister Catherine Wiggins (d. June 16, 1861, aged 47, member of Bethel) preached Sabbath afternoon Oct. 20 by Rev. James Frisby [VERIFY] before a very large audience; text Rev. xiv. 13. Obituary unsigned, dated Philada., Oct. 1861.

events.name: Trenton and Princeton circuits -- fall quarterly meetings
events.location: Mount Zion church, Trenton, N.J. (first meeting of the series)
events.description: Reported by J. P. Campbell (Phila., Nov. 7, 1861). Mount Zion, Trenton, first Saturday and Sunday of October, attended by brother Theodore Gould, preacher in charge of Princeton circuit, and brothers Redman Faucet [VERIFY], William Offere [VERIFY] and John Stephenson of Philadelphia, 'young men just entering upon the great work of the Christian ministry'. Further meetings: second Sabbath of October at Sourland Mountains [VERIFY place, read from OCR] on the Princeton circuit; third Sabbath at Louisville on the Trenton circuit (Campbell's own charge); fourth Sabbath at Pennington [VERIFY place, read from OCR], Trenton circuit, with class meeting, love-feast, sacrament.

events.name: Philadelphia District preachers' meeting
events.description: Preachers' meeting of the Philadelphia District, A. M. E. connexion. Rev. J. Eddy, President; Rev. J. Woodlin, Scribe. Reports of ministerial labors, then debate on whether Christ's sufferings equalled the Divine wrath fallen man would have endured: Revs. J. G. Bulough [VERIFY] and [initial illegible] Woodyard (printed 'C. Woodyard' in the 11-23 roster) for the affirmative; Revs. Woodlin, Cooper and Stanford for the negative. Bishop Nazrey present and took part. Question laid over as order of the day for the next meeting; adjourned to a following Tuesday, 10 1/2 A.M.

events.name: United Beneficial Sisters of Rev. J. Woodlin Society -- special meeting
events.location: Rodman St., above Ninth, Philadelphia, at Sister Dorsey's
events.description: Special meeting called by order of the President. Officers as printed: Elizabeth Harris, President; Eliza Stokelay [VERIFY], Secretary. Meeting held at the house of 'Sister Dorsey' (no given name).

events.name: Sermon on Christian Perfection, Wesley Church
events.location: Hurst street A. M. E. Wesley church, Philadelphia
events.description: Evening sermon on Christian Perfection, 7 1/2 o'clock; preacher not named.

events.name: Dorcas Society grand festival for the poor of Bethel Church
events.description: Grand festival by the ladies of the Dorcas Society; proceeds for the poor of Bethel Church; admission ten cents. Committee of arrangements as printed: Mary Sheppard, Susan Selsey [VERIFY], Mary Highgates [VERIFY], Mary E. Parker, Ann Laws, Maria Highgates [VERIFY], Elizabeth Oliver.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference -- informal meeting on Bishop Nazrey's 'double connexion' (A. M. E. / B. M. E. Church)
events.description: Called on Bishop Nazrey's notice (see CR 1861-11-02 p2 'Notice'). Members present as printed: Rev. Willis Nazrey, Bishop; Revs. R. Robinson, J. Woodlin, J. G. Buleaugh [VERIFY], S. Smith, P. Gardiner, J. P. B. Eddy, J. C. Cornish, H. Davis, S. Logan, J. P. Campbell, J. Eddy, A. L. Stanford, T. E. Jones, G. W. Johnson, Robert Evans [VERIFY], C. Woodyard; Bro. T. R. Cooper; W. D. W. Schureman. Nazrey sang part of a hymn; prayer by Rev. Richard Robinson, who on motion of Rev. J. P. Campbell was made chairman; Rev. Joshua Woodlin secretary. Campbell put the rumor that Nazrey had claimed in a public meeting at Chatham, C.W., to be Bishop of the B. M. E. Church. Nazrey answered at length, reading from the 1856 and 1860 General Conference minutes of both churches (Canadian resolutions signed by Wm. H. Jones, H. J. Young, George W. Brodie, Robert Jones; amendment of M. M. Clark; reports of Charles H. Pierce and Richard Robinson). He said he had ceased to officiate in the B. M. E. Church. Rev. Stephen Smith moved to take the sense of the house whether members were satisfied with the Bishop's statements: carried. Rev. W. D. W. Schureman moved that Rev. Willis Nazrey is a Bishop of the A. M. E. Church in America: carried. Report signed W. D. W. Schureman, Chairman; J. Woodlin, A. L. Stanford, H. Davis; J. P. Campbell, Secretary; Philadelphia, Nov. 11th [VERIFY day], 1861.
attendees: bishop (Rev.); called meeting to order and answered the inquiry
chairman (Rev.), of Frankford Circuit; opened with prayer (roster: 'R. Robinson')
member present (Rev.) (roster: 'S. Smith'); moved the sense of the house
member present (Rev.); put the questions to the Bishop; secretary of report committee
member present; moved that Nazrey is a Bishop of the A. M. E. Church in America; chairman of report committee

events.name: Frankford circuit quarterly meeting
events.description: Quarterly meeting of 'Father Robertson' (per the owner's ruling = Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford; bare surname kept in text). Love-feast 9 A.M.; discourse by Rev. Josiah Eddy 11 A.M.; Elisha Weaver preached at 2 1/2 P.M. and administered the sacrament. A Book Concern meeting followed on the next Thursday night (Nov. 14), with admission charged at the door: over three dollars taken plus book sales.
attendees: General Book Steward, preached and administered sacrament

events.name: Protracted (anxious) meeting at Union A. M. E. Church, Coates St.
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia
events.description: Revival meeting Oct. 7 to Nov. 11, 1861; 35 persons added to the church, 26 professing conversion. Reported by Henry Davis, preacher in charge.

events.name: Funeral sermon of Sister Elizabeth Williams, Wesley A.M.E. Church
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice that the funeral sermon of Sister Elizabeth Williams, deceased, would be delivered in the Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst Street, on Sabbath afternoon, the 8th instant (8 December 1861), at 3 o'clock. Preacher not named.

events.name: Executive Committee of the Book Concern -- meeting
events.description: Notice (12-14 p2) that the Executive Committee would meet in Philadelphia at 9 A.M. on 18 Dec. 1861. The 12-21 issue (p2, 'Book Concern') reports that the Executive Committee of the Book Concern met on Wednesday the 18th inst. and had a very pleasant interview with the brethren; their movements in relation to the paper to appear in the next issue. The 12-28 issue (p2, 'Resignation') reports that Rev. A. L. Stanford, acting editor since 15 July 1861, handed his resignation to the Committee on the 18th, accepted the same day, and that the Committee decided Elisha Weaver should be Editor and General Book Steward, the corps of corresponding editors remaining as before. Committee members not named.
attendees: named Editor and General Book Steward (Rev.)

events.name: Burlington Circuit quarterly meetings (Jan.-Feb. 1862)
events.location: Burlington Circuit, N.J. (Burlington, Mount Holly, Evesham, Milford, Snow Hill, Jordantown)
events.description: Schedule of quarterly meetings of the Burlington Circuit: first Sabbath in January 1862 (5 Jan.) at Burlington; second (12 Jan.) at Mount Holly; third (19 Jan.) at Evesham; fourth (26 Jan.) at Milford; first Sabbath in February (2 Feb.) at Snow Hill; second (9 Feb.) at Jordantown. Signed J. H. Smith, Elder in charge.

events.name: Bishop Willis Nazrey preaches at Wesley A.M.E. Church
events.description: Appointment: Bishop Willis Nazrey to preach in the Wesley A. M. E. Church on Sunday evening, 22 Dec. 1861, at 7 o'clock.

events.name: Elisha Weaver preaches at Union Church, Coates Street
events.description: Notice that Rev. Elisha Weaver would preach in Union Church, Coates Street, on Sabbath (22 Dec. 1861) at 3 o'clock P.M. (hour figure read as 3; faint).

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School teachers -- resolutions on the death of Rev. Walter Proctor
events.description: 'Death of Rev. Walter Proctor.' At a special meeting of teachers of Bethel Sabbath School, the Superintendent (unnamed) stated the object, to consider the demise of Rev. Walter Proctor. A committee of three, Messrs. Abraham Field and Ellis Dingle and Miss Sarah Daffin, drafted a preamble and resolutions, unanimously adopted: that the Bethel Sabbath School had lost a firm friend and faithful admonisher who, as one of the founders of the school, had been identified with all its interests from its organization to his death; condolence to the bereaved family, particularly the widow; the school-room to be draped in mourning for thirty days; resolutions to be sent to the Christian Recorder and a copy to the widow. Signed Abraham Field, Ellis Dingle, Sarah S. Daffin. Dated Philada., Dec. 16, 1861.
attendees: committee on resolutions, Bethel Sabbath School teacher
committee on resolutions, Bethel Sabbath School teacher
committee on resolutions, Bethel Sabbath School teacher (Miss; 'Sarah Daffin' in text)
deceased (Rev.); a founder of Bethel Sabbath School

events.name: Funeral of Rev. Walter Proctor, Bethel Church
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia; procession from his late residence (Rodman Street)
events.description: 'The Funeral of Rev. Walter Proctor' (signed E. W.). On Monday (printed 'the 17th inst.'; the prior notice and the calendar give Monday 16 Dec.), the ministers, trustees and stewards met in Bethel Church at half-past 11 A.M. and proceeded to his late residence, joined by a large procession that conveyed the body to Bethel Church; line of procession: Trustees, Ministers and Mourners. The church was crowded to excess. Rev. Stephen Smith gave out a hymn on the 427th page and prayed; Rev. W. D. W. Schureman read the 15th chapter of 1st Corinthians; the Bethel choir sang the funeral dirge 'Brother, thou art [wast] mild and lovely'; Rev. J. Woodlin (described as '...r' of the church, word clipped in the gutter, probably 'pastor') gave a brief sketch of the life of Father Proctor; the remains were then borne to their last resting-place.
attendees: gave sketch of the deceased's life (Rev.; probably pastor of Bethel)

events.name: Protracted meeting on the Frankford Circuit
events.description: Rev. Richard Robertson of the Frankford Circuit reported holding a protracted meeting for several weeks with many conversions; 'never was such a work in Frankford before.' (Owner's ruling: the CR's Rev. Richard Robertson is Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford.)

events.name: Rev. Alexander Crummell preaches at Bethel Church
events.description: Notice: Rev. Alexander Crummell, B. A., a missionary from Liberia, preached, as the editor was informed, in Bethel Church on Sabbath at 3 o'clock P.M. (date not given; a recent Sunday, presumably 22 Dec. 1861). The editor was not present but heard the sermon spoken of in very high terms. Crummell is a non-Philadelphian and is not linked per the extraction rule.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's visitation: Bethel and Union A.M.E. churches, Philadelphia
events.location: Bethel Church and Union A.M.E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: From Bishop Willis Nazrey's 'Episcopal Visits': after visiting Abington Centre, Wilkesbarre, Danville and Reading (Pa.), he came to Philadelphia; on Sabbath the 10th ult. [10 Nov. 1861], in the morning, he preached at Bethel Church, where many of the old veterans of the cross of former years were now hushed in death; in the evening he visited the Union A. M. E. Church and found the people with their elder enjoying themselves after the close of a very successful protracted meeting. On the next Sabbath (17 Nov.) he attended a quarterly meeting with the preacher and people (place not clear from the text). Then 22-23 Nov. at Freehold, N.J. (Brother Winder, preacher in charge; baptized seven persons aged 32 to 80), Manalapan? and Fair Hill, and on 28 Nov. at ...ville, N.J., where he joined in matrimony Mr. James Hay [VERIFY] of Freehold, N.J., and Miss Sarah Jane Williams of ...ville [VERIFY], N.J. Elder Schureman, who oversees Brother Winder, missed the quarterly meeting owing to the death and burial of his little son. Rev. J. Young (Montrose station) also named.
